evaluation_unit: one user query x one recommended book

semantic_stage.purpose: Assess every frozen query facet independently. The LLM does not assign the final 0-4 score.

support_scale.absent: No meaningful semantic support for this facet in the supplied book information.
support_scale.incidental: A genuine relationship exists, but it is peripheral, superficial, or not an important part of the described book.
support_scale.meaningful: The description substantively supports the facet. Support may be implicit when reasonably entailed by the text, but must not rely on speculation or external knowledge.
support_scale.strong: The facet is directly, explicitly, and centrally supported by the supplied description.

instructions: Evaluate semantic recommendation relevance only.
Use only the supplied query, frozen facets, title, authors, description, rubric, and these instructions.
Do not use external knowledge about the book, author, series, historical events, or cultural context.
Treat the description as the primary evidence source. Title and authors may provide supporting context but must not override the description.
Assess every supplied facet independently.
Do not invent, merge, remove, or rewrite facets.
A strong match on one facet does not imply support for another facet.
A missing facet does not erase genuine support for another facet.
Do not reward isolated keyword overlap when the described meaning is unrelated.
Reasonable semantic entailment is allowed. The description does not need to contain the exact facet wording.
Do not infer plausible but unstated themes, motivations, plot events, or relationships.
Use incidental when a real relationship exists but the facet is peripheral or superficial.
Use meaningful when the facet is substantively supported even if the wording is indirect.
Use strong only when the facet is direct, explicit, and central.
Use absent when no meaningful semantic relationship is supported.
Give a concise reason for each facet tied to the supplied description.
Return exactly one assessment for each supplied facet and no others.
Do not output an overall numeric score or overall match label.

rules.1_incidental: At least one core facet is incidental, but no core facet is meaningful or strong.
rules.2_partial: At least one core facet is meaningful or strong, but fewer than two-thirds of core facets are meaningful or strong.
rules.3_clear: At least two-thirds of core facets are meaningful or strong, but all core facets are not strong.
rules.qualifier_cap: If a provisional score is 4 and any qualifier is below meaningful, cap the final score at 3.

scoring_stage.tie_break_rule: Choose the lower score unless the deterministic conditions for the higher score are satisfied.

evidence_stage.purpose: After semantic support levels are frozen, Python numbers exact description spans and the LLM selects one supporting span ID for every non-absent facet. Python then persists the exact source text for the selected ID.
instructions: Evidence selection happens only after facet support has been decided.
The model selects a supplied source span ID rather than generating or copying quote text.
Return exactly one valid source span ID for every non-absent facet.
The selected span need not contain the facet's exact words; reasonable semantic entailment is allowed.
Do not select a span based only on unrelated keyword overlap.
Do not invent span IDs.
Do not change facet support, facet reason, or the deterministic score.
Python retrieves the exact evidence text from the selected source span.
